title: Canonical split top cancellation homotopy
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $B$ an integer-indexed cochain complex of $\mathcal O_S$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. For $m\in\mathbb N$, suppose $B$ is supported in degrees at most $m+1$ and its differential $\delta:B^m\to B^{m+1}$ has a right inverse. The canonical truncation $\tau_{\le m}B$ (cycles in degree $m$, the original terms below $m$, and zero terms above $m$) is chain homotopy equivalent to $B$.

source.place: Tags 068V and 00MT; explicit categorical split identity-pair cancellation expanding the planned argument

proof.text: Choose a section σ of the split epimorphism δ. Define the degree-minus-one family h with σ in degree m+1 to m and zero elsewhere. Mathlib Homotopy.nullHomotopicMap h is a chain map N = dh+hd and Homotopy.nullHomotopy h proves N is homotopic to zero. Put p = id-N. At degree m+1 the section equation makes p zero; above m+1 the support hypothesis makes it zero.

The canonical inclusion i of truncLE m into B satisfies i composed with p = i. Below m the homotopy boundary vanishes. At m, the chain-map equation for i and the zero term of the truncation at m+1 show i_m δ=0. Above m the source of i is zero.

Factor p through its abelian image I with epimorphism e and monomorphism j. Each I term above m is zero: cancel e and j in e_i j_i=p_i=0 to obtain id_{I_i}=0. Therefore the canonical inclusion of truncLE m I is an isomorphism. Set g=e composed with its inverse composed with truncLEMap j. Truncation naturality gives g composed with i=p.

Cancel the monomorphism i in i composed with g composed with i=i composed with p=i to obtain i composed with g=id. Negate the null homotopy of N and add the identity homotopy to obtain a homotopy p~id. Using g composed with i=p yields the second inverse homotopy. Assemble HomotopyEquiv with hom=i and inv=g.

proof_origin.place: Tags 068V and 00MT; explicit split identity-pair contraction; H2 uses the abelian image of id-dh-hd to factor through canonical truncation
